title: Seven failure stories, one evidence conflict, and overlapping mandatory actions

application.name: Northstar Pilot
application.description: An invite-only order and support assistant intended to become a public product.

data_summary: Names, email addresses, order history, support messages and hosted-checkout payment references for named pilot users.

extra_evidence.scope: The handler calls an ownership helper, but the live two-account test below contradicts the helper's expected behavior.

findings.rationale: A second pilot account retrieved the first account's order by changing the order id.

evidence.scope: One known private order in the pilot environment; no writes were attempted.

conflicts.resolution: The code shape is only indicative; the scoped live cross-account result decides this assessment.

findings.rationale: A provider credential is committed in the current branch.

evidence.scope: Current branch and reachable history; the secret value is redacted.

findings.rationale: The metered model account has no monthly or per-user cap.

evidence.scope: The production-bound provider account settings reviewed with the owner.

findings.rationale: No restore has ever been attempted from the database backups.

evidence.scope: Runbooks and provider activity available during the review.

findings.rationale: Unhandled server errors are printed to a console nobody monitors.
Support prompts copy full order records although only the order state is needed.

evidence.scope: The server prompt builder and one redacted trace.

findings.rationale: Customer messages and operator instructions are concatenated into one prompt without a trust boundary.

actions.outcome: Contain the cross-account order exposure and determine which records were accessed.
actions.reason: The authorized test demonstrated access across account boundaries.

deadline.rationale: The exposure exists in the running pilot.

actions.success_evidence: Access is denied in a repeated two-account test, affected access is reviewed, and the control is reassessed.

actions.outcome: Collect a bounded error-path inventory for the developer to instrument.
actions.reason: The current scan shows no monitored error path.

deadline.rationale: Failures must be observable before public use.

actions.success_evidence: The inventory names every reviewed server error path and its current handling.

actions.outcome: Decide and document which order fields the support assistant is allowed to receive.
actions.reason: The owner must define the minimum necessary data before the code can enforce it.

deadline.rationale: The data contract must precede public use.

actions.success_evidence: A reviewed field allowlist and retention statement are recorded.

actions.outcome: Refactor the test-data helper when the next test suite cleanup is scheduled.
actions.reason: The helper is awkward but does not block any assessed scope.

deadline.rationale: No current environment or intended use depends on it.

actions.success_evidence: The helper has focused tests and no duplicated setup.

procedures.title: Disable the affected order endpoint and deploy an authorization fix

authorization.scope: The affected endpoint and its deployment only.

failure_behavior.rollback: Redeploy the last known version with the endpoint disabled.

procedures.success_evidence: A repeated two-account test denies cross-account reads.

procedures.title: Scan and review server error paths
procedures.success_evidence: A bounded path-and-handler inventory with review notes.

baseline.rationale: The remaining Critical and High controls were reviewed with the owner and no contrary evidence was found.
baseline.screening_rationale: The owner answered the screening question; no specialist escalation was identified for this pilot.

evidence.scope: The current working tree and project settings visible during the 16 August review.
